name: cjk_bigram_confusion_memory
hypothesis: Replacing the ASCII-only tokenizer ([A-Za-z0-9]+) with CJK character bigrams gives non-degenerate similarity scores over Chinese legal text, restoring the confusion disambiguation retrieval mechanism so it surfaces genuinely relevant examples instead of random ones.

name: label_glossary_memory
hypothesis: Accumulating canonical ground-truth label strings during training and injecting them as a reference glossary section in the prompt anchors the LLM to exact label forms, reducing surface-form near-miss and specificity errors that account for a large share of the base system's wrong predictions.

name: confusion_lesson_memory
hypothesis: For each wrong prediction, calling the LLM once to distill a corrective lesson ('when you see X prefer Y over Z because...') and injecting the top-k most similar lessons as an explicit advisory section in the prompt will reduce fine-grained charge confusion errors that raw Q/A examples cannot encode as explicit rules.

name: mmr_diversity_memory
hypothesis: Replacing Jaccard top-k retrieval with Maximal Marginal Relevance (lam=0.6) will reduce multi-label omissions by ensuring the retrieved example set spans multiple charge families rather than clustering around one neighbourhood, giving the LLM at least one multi-charge exemplar when the query facts describe concurrent behaviours.
